why_en: Tiered shedding ranks writes by business value: clicks drive billing and attribution, while dropping impressions for a while only blurs reach estimates — at the cost of a gap in impression counts.
tradeoff: 保住高价值写 vs 指标完整性
whenOtherWins: 如果下游主要看 CTR（点击率），分母缺失会让比率失真，这时对两类同比例采样才是对的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告被展示一次的事件，量大但单条价值低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one event recording that an ad was displayed — high volume, low value per record.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点击广告的事件，直接关联计费和转化归因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A click event records that a user clicked an ad, and it ties directly to billing and conversion attribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率，等于点击数除以曝光数，衡量广告效果的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR, or click-through rate, is clicks divided by impressions and is the core measure of ad effectiveness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次成交归到具体哪次广告点击上的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Conversion attribution assigns a purchase back to the specific ad click that produced it.

optionExplanations: 同比例采样保住了比率，却让高价值的 click 也一起丢，计费和归因直接出现漏账。
click 与钱直接挂钩，impression 只是估算基数，按价值排序就该先牺牲后者。
误解：排队不减总量，超出稳态吞吐时队列只会积压，click 的落库反而更晚。
误解：判断依据是业务价值不是数量，click 稀少恰恰说明每条都更贵重。
optionExplanations_en: Uniform sampling preserves the ratio but throws away high-value clicks too, punching holes in billing and attribution.
Clicks map straight to money while impressions are only an estimation base, so value ordering sacrifices impressions first.
Misconception: queueing does not reduce total volume — past steady-state capacity the backlog just grows and clicks land even later.
Misconception: the criterion is business value, not count; clicks being rare is exactly why each one is worth more.

scenario: 订单分析服务已经分了片、加了队列，数据库仍是写瓶颈；每条写都要一次网络往返、一次事务建立和一轮索引更新。
scenario_en: An order-analytics service is already sharded and queued but the database is still the write bottleneck; every single write costs a network round trip, a transaction setup, and an index update.
q: 除了接受既有写量之外还有哪条路？
q_en: Beyond accepting the existing write volume, what other lever is left?
options: 改变写的结构，把多条写合成一批，摊薄每条写的固定开销
继续增加分片数量，把同样多的写摊到更多机器上面去
给数据库加只读副本，把压力从主库整体转移出去处理
把队列的分区数继续调大，提高消费者并行度，让积压更快被排空
options_en: Change the shape of the writes: merge many writes into one batch to amortize the per-write fixed cost
Keep adding shards so the same write volume is spread across more machines
Add read replicas so pressure is moved off the primary database
Raise the queue partition count to increase consumer parallelism and drain the backlog faster
why: 分片和队列都只是把既有写量搬来搬去；批处理直接减少写的条数——网络往返、事务建立、索引更新是每条写的固定开销，合批即摊薄。代价是多一层延迟。
why_en: Sharding and queueing only move a fixed write volume around, while batching reduces the number of writes so the fixed per-write cost is amortized — at the price of added latency.
tradeoff: 合批摊薄固定开销 vs 引入缓冲延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果写是互不相关的单键随机写、根本攒不出同键批，合批毫无压缩，只能靠分片继续摊。

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条写都要付的一次性成本：网络往返、事务建立、索引更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fixed per-write overhead is the cost every single write pays: a network round trip, transaction setup, and index maintenance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库为一次写开启事务、加锁、写日志的准备工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transaction setup is the work a database does to open a transaction, take locks, and log before a write commits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库的只读复制实例，用来分摊读流量，不能分摊写提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the primary that offloads reads but cannot offload write commits.

optionExplanations: 合批把 N 次事务建立和索引更新压成 1 次，减少的是写的条数本身，不是分布位置。
误解：分片只改变写落在哪台机器，每条写的固定开销一分不少地照付。
误解：副本只能分摊读，写提交仍全部落在主库，写瓶颈原样不动。
误解：调分区数提高的是消费并行度，数据库仍要逐条承接同样多的写。
optionExplanations_en: Batching collapses N transaction setups and index updates into one, cutting the write count itself rather than relocating it.
Misconception: sharding only changes which machine a write lands on; each write still pays its full fixed overhead.
Misconception: replicas offload reads only — every commit still hits the primary, so the write bottleneck is untouched.
Misconception: more partitions raise consumer parallelism, but the database still absorbs the same number of individual writes.

scenario: 一个服务从 Kafka topic 读事件、处理后写库。有人提议在应用进程内先攒 500 条再一次性提交数据库。
scenario_en: A service reads events from a Kafka topic, processes them, and writes to a database; someone proposes buffering 500 writes in the process before committing them together.
q: 这个应用层批处理为什么可以安全采用？
q_en: Why is this application-layer batching safe to adopt?
options: 应用不是权威数据源，崩了重读 Kafka 就能恢复这一批
批量提交在数据库里是原子的，所以任何崩溃都不可能造成丢数据
Kafka 已经把消息持久化了，所以数据库这边不需要再关心提交顺序
攒批只是把写延后，应用崩溃时操作系统会把缓冲区自动刷进数据库里
options_en: The app is not the authoritative store, so after a crash it re-reads Kafka to rebuild the batch
A batch commit is atomic in the database, so no crash can ever lose data
Kafka already persisted the messages, so the database side no longer has to care about commit ordering
Batching only delays writes, and on a crash the OS flushes the buffer into the database automatically
why: 攒批安不安全取决于谁是 source of truth：数据还在 Kafka 里，进程崩了从 offset 重读即可。代价是重放会重复投递，写入必须幂等。
why_en: Whether batching is safe depends on who owns the source of truth: the data still lives in Kafka, so a crashed process just re-reads from its offset — at the cost of needing idempotent writes.
tradeoff: 攒批省下的提交次数 vs 崩溃后重放与幂等要求
whenOtherWins: 如果应用本身就是 source of truth（直接接用户请求并已回执成功），应用层攒批就不安全，得改用中间批处理进程。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据的权威副本所在处，丢了就无处可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is where the authoritative copy of data lives — if it is lost, there is nowhere to recover it from.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 分区中每条消息的位置编号，消费者靠它记住读到哪了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka offset is the position number of a message in a partition, letting a consumer remember where it left off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个操作重复执行多次，结果与执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating the same operation many times leaves the same result as doing it once.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 中一类消息的持久化日志通道，可按 offset 重复读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka topic is a durable log channel of messages that can be re-read from any offset.

optionExplanations: 上游日志保留了原始事件，重启后从上次 offset 重读就能补齐未提交的那批。
误解：原子的是「已发出的那次提交」，还没发出的内存批不在数据库的保护范围内。
误解：这题问的是丢不丢数据，提交顺序是另一个话题，不能解释为什么安全。
误解：内存里的应用级缓冲不是操作系统页缓存，进程一没，这批数据就没了。
optionExplanations_en: The upstream log still holds the raw events, so on restart the service re-reads from its last offset and rebuilds the uncommitted batch.
Misconception: atomicity covers a commit that was actually issued; an in-memory batch never sent is outside the database protection.
Misconception: the question is about data loss — commit ordering is a separate topic and does not explain safety.
Misconception: an application-level buffer is not the OS page cache; when the process dies the batch dies with it.

scenario: 一个直接接收用户下单请求的服务，收到请求就返回成功，并把写攒进内存批，每 2 秒提交一次数据库。
scenario_en: A service takes user order requests directly, returns success immediately, buffers writes in an in-memory batch, and commits to the database every 2 seconds.
q: 进程在提交前崩溃会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the process crashes before the batch commits?
options: 已向用户确认成功的那批写随进程一起消失，且无处可重放
写会留在数据库连接池的缓冲里，进程重启后自动补提交上去
客户端会收到超时错误，因此可以安全重试，不存在丢数据窗口
数据库的 WAL（预写日志）里已有这批写的记录，重启后可回放恢复
options_en: The batch already acknowledged to users vanishes with the process, and there is nothing upstream to replay
The writes stay in the connection pool buffer and are committed automatically after restart
Clients get a timeout error and can safely retry, so there is no data-loss window
The database write-ahead log already holds these writes, so a restart can replay them
why: 正常路径：用户拿到成功回执但写只在内存。进程崩溃 → 这批写既没入库也没有上游日志可重读 → 用户看到订单凭空消失。应用是 source of truth 时不能无脑攒批。
why_en: The user already holds a success receipt while the write lives only in memory, so a crash leaves it neither committed nor replayable and the order simply disappears — never batch blindly when the app is the source of truth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据的权威副本所在处，丢了就无处可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is where the authoritative copy of data lives — if it is lost, there is nowhere to recover it from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库在改数据页之前先写的持久化日志，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log, or WAL, is the durable log a database writes before touching data pages, used for crash recovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用数据库连接的客户端组件，只管连接，不保证写的持久化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool reuses database connections on the client side; it manages connections and guarantees nothing about durability.

optionExplanations: 成功回执已经发出，数据却只在进程内存里，上游又没有日志可重读，这是真正的丢数据。
误解：连接池只复用 TCP 连接，不缓存也不重发未提交的业务写。
误解：客户端早已拿到 200 成功回执，压根不会重试，问题正出在这里。
误解：WAL 只保护「已经到达数据库」的写，还在应用内存里的批从没到过数据库。
optionExplanations_en: The success receipt is already out while the data sits only in process memory with no upstream log to replay — that is genuine data loss.
Misconception: a connection pool reuses TCP connections; it neither caches nor resends uncommitted business writes.
Misconception: the client already got a 200 success and will never retry — that is precisely the problem.
Misconception: the WAL only protects writes that reached the database; a batch still in application memory never got there.

scenario: Like Batcher 是写路径上的中间聚合进程：它收 Like 事件，在窗口内按帖子累加计数，再写库。某热帖 1 分钟收到 100 个赞，窗口设为 1 分钟。
scenario_en: A Like Batcher is an intermediate process on the write path: it consumes like events, tallies counts per post inside a window, then writes to the database. One hot post gets 100 likes in a minute with a 1-minute window.
q: 这一分钟里落到数据库的写次数是多少？
q_en: How many database writes land during that minute?
options: 压到 1 次：窗口内 100 个赞聚合成一条计数更新，压缩比 100:1
仍然是 100 次：中间批处理只是把写延后，并不会减少最终落库的写次数
变成 0 次：计数只留在批处理进程内存里，靠读时再实时算
变成 101 次：100 条原始事件加 1 条聚合结果全都要写库
options_en: Down to one: the 100 likes in the window collapse into a single count update, a 100:1 compression ratio
Still one hundred: intermediate batching only defers writes and never reduces how many finally land
Down to zero: the count stays in the batcher memory and is computed at read time
Up to one hundred and one: the 100 raw events plus the aggregate all get written
why: 库写次数 = 帖子数 × 窗口数，与赞的条数无关：1 帖 × 1 窗口 = 1 次写；压缩比 = 100 赞 ÷ 1 次写 = 100:1。这个比值是判断批处理值不值得做的依据。
why_en: Database writes equal posts times windows, not likes: one post times one window is one write, so the compression ratio is 100 likes over 1 write — that ratio is what tells you whether batching is worth it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径上的中间进程，在时间窗口内把同一帖子的点赞累加成一次计数更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Like Batcher is an intermediate process that tallies likes for the same post inside a time window into one count update.

termDefinitions.meaning: 窗口内进来的事件数除以实际落库的写次数，衡量批处理收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The compression ratio is events entering a window divided by writes actually committed, measuring how much batching buys you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 批处理器攒事件的时间长度，窗口越长压缩越多、延迟越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The batching window is how long the batcher accumulates events; longer windows compress more but add latency.

optionExplanations: 同一帖子的赞在窗口内累加，只有最终计数需要落库，所以是 1 次写。
误解：中间批处理不是延后逐条写，而是把同键事件合并成一条计数更新。
误解：批处理器只是缓冲，窗口结束必须把结果写库，否则崩了计数就没了。
误解：原始事件在这条路径上并不落库，Like Batcher 保留的是计数不是明细。
optionExplanations_en: Likes for the same post accumulate inside the window and only the final count is committed, so it is a single write.
Misconception: intermediate batching does not defer per-event writes, it merges same-key events into one count update.
Misconception: the batcher is only a buffer — at window close it must commit, or the count dies with a crash.
Misconception: raw events are not persisted on this path; the Like Batcher keeps the count, not the detail rows.

scenario: 同一套 Like Batcher 换个场景：绝大多数帖子每小时才收到 1 个赞，聚合窗口仍设为 1 分钟。
scenario_en: The same Like Batcher in a different setting: most posts get just one like per hour, while the aggregation window is still one minute.
q: 这时批处理带来的收益是多少？
q_en: How much benefit does batching deliver here?
options: 几乎为零：每个窗口通常只有 1 个赞，聚合不掉任何写
仍有 60 倍收益，因为一小时的赞会被压成 1 次写入操作
收益更大，帖子越冷批处理器内存占用越低，压缩得越充分
收益不变，批处理的压缩比只取决于窗口长度，与事件到达速率无关
options_en: Almost none: each window usually holds a single like, so nothing gets merged away
Still a 60x win, because an hour of likes collapses into one write
Even better: colder posts use less batcher memory and therefore compress more
Unchanged: the compression ratio depends only on window length, not on arrival rate
why: 压缩比 = 窗口内同键事件数；到达率低于每窗口 1 条时压缩比约等于 1，等于白加了一分钟延迟。上批处理之前必须先验证到达率。
why_en: Compression equals same-key events per window, so when arrivals fall below one per window the ratio is about one and you have bought only a minute of latency — validate arrival rate before batching.
tradeoff: 写次数压缩 vs 额外延迟与多一个活动组件
whenOtherWins: 把窗口拉到 1 小时压缩比才起来，但写入可见延迟也变成 1 小时，实时计数场景不可接受。

termDefinitions.meaning: 窗口内进来的事件数除以实际落库的写次数，衡量批处理收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The compression ratio is events entering a window divided by writes actually committed, measuring how much batching buys you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内某个键收到的事件条数，决定窗口内能攒到几条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Arrival rate is how many events a given key receives per unit time, which decides how many can accumulate in a window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要部署、监控和故障处理的额外运行进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A moving part is an extra running component that must be deployed, monitored, and recovered when it fails.

optionExplanations: 窗口内攒不到第二条同键事件，1 条进 1 条出，写次数一点没少。
误解：60 倍要求这一小时的赞落在同一个窗口里，1 分钟窗口根本装不下一小时。
误解：省内存不等于省写入，这题问的是落库写次数有没有减少。
误解：压缩比是「窗口长度 × 到达率」，到达率趋近 0 时窗口再长也压不动。
optionExplanations_en: No second same-key event ever lands in the window, so one in means one out and the write count is unchanged.
Misconception: a 60x win requires an hour of likes inside one window, and a one-minute window cannot span an hour.
Misconception: saving memory is not saving writes — the question is whether committed write count drops.
Misconception: compression is window length times arrival rate; as arrivals approach zero, no window length helps.

scenario: 写吞吐仍不够，有人提议直接调数据库自身的刷盘频率（Redis 默认每 100ms 把写刷一次盘）来吸收写压力。
scenario_en: Throughput is still short and someone proposes tuning the database own flush interval — Redis flushes writes to disk every 100ms by default — to absorb the pressure.
q: 该怎么评价这个数据库层批处理？
q_en: How should you judge this database-layer batching?
options: 可行但是「大锤」：它改的是全库持久化行为，只留给极端情况
首选方案：不用改任何应用代码，风险最低，应当第一个尝试
无效：刷盘频率只影响读延迟，对写入吞吐没有任何实际影响
等价于应用层批处理，只是换个地方做，收益和风险其实完全一样
options_en: Workable but a big hammer: it changes durability for the whole database, so reserve it for extreme cases
The first choice: no application code changes, lowest risk, so try it first
Useless: flush frequency only affects read latency and does nothing for write throughput
Equivalent to application-layer batching, just done elsewhere, with identical benefit and risk
why: 调刷盘频率把攒批下沉到存储引擎，影响的是整库的持久化窗口——崩溃会丢掉这 100ms 内所有键的写。粒度最粗，所以是最后手段。
why_en: Tuning flush interval pushes batching down into the storage engine and widens the durability window for the entire database, so a crash loses every key written in those 100ms — it is a last resort.
tradeoff: 拉长刷盘间隔换写吞吐 vs 崩溃丢失窗口变大
whenOtherWins: 当上游写来自大量互不相关的键、根本攒不出同键批时，数据库层反而是唯一还能调的地方。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内存中已接受的写真正落到磁盘的动作，多数系统的吞吐瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk flush pushes accepted in-memory writes onto durable storage, and it is the throughput bottleneck for most systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存数据结构存储，常用作缓存和高频计数器，可配置刷盘频率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory data-structure store used for caching and high-frequency counters, with a configurable flush interval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写被接受但尚未落盘的时间段，崩溃时这段内的写会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The durability window is the span in which writes are accepted but not yet on disk, and a crash loses everything inside it.

optionExplanations: 这个旋钮一拧全库都受影响，没法只对热点键生效，所以只在别的层都用尽后才动。
误解：不改代码不等于低风险，它换来的是全库范围的数据丢失窗口变大。
误解：刷盘正是多数系统的写瓶颈，攒批刷盘直接影响可持续写入速率。
误解：应用层能挑哪些写攒批，数据库层只能一刀切，风险面完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: This knob affects the entire database and cannot be scoped to hot keys, so it comes only after the other layers are exhausted.
Misconception: not touching code is not low risk — it buys a wider data-loss window across the whole database.
Misconception: disk flushing is exactly the write bottleneck for most systems, so batching flushes moves sustainable write rate.
Misconception: the application layer chooses which writes to batch; the database layer is all-or-nothing, a very different risk surface.

scenario: 直播平台每秒收到数百万条点赞与评论事件，产品只需要展示实时的总计数和最新评论列表，不需要回放每条原始事件。
scenario_en: A live-streaming platform takes millions of like and comment events per second, and the product only needs live totals and the latest comments — never a replay of each raw event.
q: 为什么这里可以做层级聚合？
q_en: Why does hierarchical aggregation apply here?
options: 因为只需要聚合视图，而聚合视图能分阶段增量构建，逐级减量
因为事件量大到必须完整保存每条原始事件，聚合只是加速读取用的索引
因为聚合能保证强一致，比直接写原始事件的一致性更好一些
因为观众数量少于事件数量，所以扇出天然不构成瓶颈问题
options_en: Because only an aggregated view is needed, and such a view can be built incrementally, shrinking volume at each stage
Because the volume forces you to keep every raw event, and the aggregate is just an index that speeds reads up
Because aggregation guarantees strong consistency, which beats writing raw events directly
Because there are fewer viewers than events, so fan-out is not a bottleneck to begin with
why: 高量流数据的前提是下游只要聚合结果、不要每条明细，于是每一级都能先减量再上送。代价是每加一级就多一跳延迟。
why_en: The premise for high-volume stream data is that downstream only needs the aggregate, so each stage can reduce volume before forwarding — each extra stage costs one more hop of latency.
tradeoff: 逐级减量的吞吐 vs 多跳带来的延迟
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要审计或回放每条原始事件（合规、计费明细），中间层就不能丢明细，只能全量落库。

termDefinitions.meaning: 分多级处理数据，每级把事件量减少后再转给上一级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hierarchical aggregation processes data in stages, reducing event volume at each level before forwarding it upward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只保留统计结果（计数、总和）而不保留每条原始事件的数据视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregated view keeps only summary results like counts and sums rather than every raw event.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每来一批新事件就在已有结果上累加，而不是重算全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Incremental build adds each new batch onto the existing result instead of recomputing everything from scratch.

optionExplanations: 计数和最新评论都能在上送前先在本级合并，量级一级比一级小，这正是分层的前提。
误解：正好相反，能丢掉原始明细才是层级聚合成立的条件。
误解：分层聚合走的是最终一致路线，多加几跳只会让收敛更晚，不会更强一致。
误解：直播的痛点恰恰是百万观众对百万写者的全对全扇出，扇出正是瓶颈本身。
optionExplanations_en: Counts and latest comments can both be merged locally before forwarding, so volume shrinks stage by stage — that is the precondition.
Misconception: the opposite is true — being allowed to discard raw detail is what makes hierarchical aggregation possible.
Misconception: staged aggregation is an eventually-consistent design; extra hops delay convergence rather than strengthening consistency.
Misconception: the pain in live streams is exactly the all-to-all fan-out among millions of viewers, so fan-out is the bottleneck.

scenario: 直播间百万观众，每人发的评论都要推给所有其他人，构成全对全扇出；所有观众要的是同一份最终一致的视图。
scenario_en: A live room with a million viewers needs every comment pushed to everyone else, an all-to-all fan-out, and all viewers want the same eventually consistent view.
q: 怎么把读侧的全对全扇出降下来？
q_en: How do you cut down the all-to-all fan-out on the read side?
options: 写到 M 个广播节点，由它们各自扇出给名下的观众
给每个观众各建一条独立投递队列，逐个精确推送每一条新评论
让观众定时轮询数据库拉最新评论，把扇出压力整体转成读压力
按观众 ID 把评论分片存储，让每个观众只从自己那一片读所需数据
options_en: Write to M broadcast nodes and let each fan out to the viewers assigned to it
Give every viewer a dedicated delivery queue and push each new comment to them one by one
Have viewers poll the database periodically, converting all fan-out pressure into read pressure
Shard comments by viewer ID so each viewer reads only from their own slice of the data
why: 全对全的前提是每个写者直接找每个读者；改成写 M 个广播节点后写扇出从 N 降到 M，观众用 consistent hashing 分配到节点。代价是多一跳延迟。
why_en: All-to-all assumes every writer reaches every reader; writing to M broadcast nodes instead drops fan-out from N to M, with viewers assigned by consistent hashing, at the cost of one more hop.
tradeoff: 写扇出从 N 降到 M vs 多一跳延迟与广播节点运维
whenOtherWins: 如果每个观众要的是各自不同的定制视图，广播节点无法复用同一份更新，逐人投递反而更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收更新后转发给挂在自己名下那批观众的中间节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broadcast node receives updates and forwards them to the set of viewers assigned to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把键映射到环上节点的哈希方式，增删节点时只需搬动少量映射。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys onto a ring of nodes so that adding or removing a node moves only a small share of the mappings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条写需要投递到多少个接收方，接收方越多写放大越严重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is how many recipients one write must be delivered to; more recipients means more write amplification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内读可能读到旧值，但最终会收敛到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read right after a write may be stale, but the system converges to the latest value.

optionExplanations: 观众都要同一份视图，所以一份更新可以在广播节点上复用给它名下的所有人。
误解：每人一条队列就是把 N 路扇出原样写下来，一点没减少写放大。
误解：百万观众高频轮询会把压力搬到数据库上，扇出并没有消失只是换了受害者。
误解：按观众 ID 分片要求同一条评论复制进每个观众的分片，写放大反而更大。
optionExplanations_en: All viewers want the same view, so one update can be reused on a broadcast node for everyone assigned to it.
Misconception: a queue per viewer just spells out the N-way fan-out literally and removes no write amplification.
Misconception: a million viewers polling frequently moves the load onto the database — fan-out did not vanish, it changed victims.
Misconception: sharding by viewer ID requires copying each comment into every viewer slice, which amplifies writes further.

scenario: 直播评论加了广播节点后读侧扇出解决了，但所有观众的评论与点赞事件仍然全部打到同一个 root processor。
scenario_en: Broadcast nodes fixed the read-side fan-out for live comments, but every viewer comment and like event still lands on the single root processor.
q: 上游该怎么再减一层写压力？
q_en: How do you shed one more layer of write pressure upstream?
options: 上游加一层 write processor，按评论 ID 路由并窗口聚合后上送
给 root processor 加只读副本，把聚合压力分摊到副本上面去做
让广播节点直接互相同步，彻底去掉 root processor 这个角色
把 root processor 垂直扩容到更大机型，并在它前面加一层写队列做缓冲
options_en: Add a write-processor tier upstream that routes by comment ID and forwards window aggregates
Add read replicas to the root processor so the aggregation load spreads onto the replicas
Let broadcast nodes sync directly with each other and drop the root processor entirely
Vertically scale the root processor to a bigger instance and put a write queue in front of it as a buffer
why: 事件按评论 ID 路由到固定的 write processor，它在窗口内聚合该评论的点赞与评论数，批量上送，root 只做 merge。代价是又多一跳延迟。
why_en: Events route by comment ID to a fixed write processor that aggregates that comment over a window and forwards batches, leaving the root to merely merge — at the cost of another hop of latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按键路由接收事件、在窗口内聚合后再上送的中间处理节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write processor receives events routed by key, aggregates them over a window, and forwards the result upward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 层级聚合最顶层的节点，负责合并各下级送上来的聚合结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The root processor sits at the top of the hierarchy and merges the aggregates sent up by lower tiers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个已聚合的部分结果合并成一份全局结果的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Merging combines several partially aggregated results into one global result.

optionExplanations: 按评论 ID 路由保证同一条评论的事件落在同一个处理器，才能在本级先合并再上送。
误解：副本只帮读，聚合是写路径上的工作，root 收到的事件条数一条不少。
误解：去掉 root 后每个广播节点都要和其它所有节点同步，又变回全对全。
误解：更大机型和队列都不减少事件条数，稳态超载时只是把积压换个地方存。
optionExplanations_en: Routing by comment ID keeps all events for one comment on the same processor, which is what lets it merge locally before forwarding.
Misconception: replicas only help reads; aggregation is write-path work and the root still receives every event.
Misconception: dropping the root forces every broadcast node to sync with every other one, recreating all-to-all.
Misconception: a bigger box and a queue reduce no events — under sustained overload they only relocate the backlog.

scenario: 你打算在设计里同时用上队列、分区和批处理，面试官要求先讲清每项各自的代价再动手。
scenario_en: You plan to use queues, partitioning, and batching together in one design, and the interviewer asks you to state each cost before you propose it.
q: 下面哪些「策略 → 代价」的搭配是对的？（多选）
q_en: Which strategy-to-cost pairings are correct? (select all)
options: 队列：写入变最终一致，客户端要另外回查确认写是否落库
分区：读路径可能受损，跨分区查询要扇出到所有分片再合并结果
批处理：引入额外延迟，并多出一个必须部署和监控的活动组件
队列：能同时提升写吞吐和读一致性，几乎没有需要说明的代价
options_en: Queues: writes become eventually consistent, so clients need a callback to confirm the write landed
Partitioning: the read path can suffer, since cross-partition queries fan out to every shard and merge
Batching: it adds latency and introduces one more moving part to deploy and monitor
Queues: they raise write throughput and read consistency at once, with essentially no cost to mention
why: 三条路都在减少单个组件承担的吞吐，代价各不相同：队列=最终一致+延迟，分区=读路径受损，批处理=延迟+活动组件。先讲代价再提方案。
why_en: All three reduce throughput per component but each has its own cost: queues bring eventual consistency and delay, partitioning compromises the read path, batching adds latency and moving parts — name the cost before proposing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内读可能读到旧值，但最终会收敛到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read right after a write may be stale, but the system converges to the latest value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次查询要发到所有分片再把结果合并，延迟取决于最慢的那片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scatter-gather query goes to every shard and merges results, so its latency is set by the slowest shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要部署、监控和故障处理的额外运行进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A moving part is an extra running component that must be deployed, monitored, and recovered when it fails.

optionExplanations: 队列把「接受写」和「写库」解耦，压力削峰了，但客户端只知入队，需要回查确认。
分区按写均匀铺开，代价是不按分区键的查询要打到每一片，延迟取决于最慢分片。
批处理减的是写的条数，代价是要等窗口关闭，还多一个进程要运维。
误解：队列不改善一致性，它恰恰把强一致确认换成了异步的最终一致。
optionExplanations_en: A queue decouples accepting a write from committing it, smoothing peaks, but the client only knows it was enqueued and must check back.
Partitioning spreads writes evenly at the cost of queries off the partition key hitting every shard, with latency set by the slowest.
Batching cuts the number of writes, paying with the wait for the window to close plus one more process to operate.
Misconception: queues do not improve consistency — they trade a strongly consistent acknowledgment for asynchronous eventual consistency.

scenario: 线上 8 个分片写满要扩到 16 个。有人提议停服，把全量数据按新的 hash 重算后搬到新分片，再开服。
scenario_en: Eight shards are saturated and must become sixteen; someone proposes taking the system offline, rehashing all data onto the new shards, then reopening.
q: 这个朴素 resharding 在大数据集上会怎么破？
q_en: How does this naive resharding break on a large dataset?
options: hash 结果几乎全变，绝大多数数据都要搬，大数据集意味着数小时停机
只有一半的数据需要搬动，因此停机时间可以控制在分钟级别里面
数据不用搬，客户端换个 hash 函数就能直接找到新分片上的数据
搬迁期间写入会自动排队缓冲，服务不中断，用户完全感知不到影响
options_en: Nearly every hash result changes, so almost all data must move, and a large dataset means hours of downtime
Only half the data needs to move, so downtime stays in the minutes range
No data moves at all: clients just switch hash functions and find data on the new shards
Writes are queued automatically during the move, service stays up, and users notice nothing
why: 分片数从 8 变 16，key 到分片的映射对绝大多数 key 都变了，等于全量重排；停服期间读写全不可用，数据集越大停机越久。这就是朴素方案不能上生产的原因。
why_en: Going from 8 shards to 16 changes the key-to-shard mapping for almost every key, so it is a full reshuffle with reads and writes unavailable throughout, and the bigger the dataset the longer the outage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改变分片数量并把数据重新分配到新分片集合的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resharding changes the number of shards and redistributes data across the new set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按新的分片数重新计算每个 key 归属哪个分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rehashing recomputes which shard each key belongs to under the new shard count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务对外完全不可用的时间段，迁移期间读写都被拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Downtime is the period when the service is fully unavailable and both reads and writes are refused.

optionExplanations: 映射变了就得逐条搬，数据量决定搬迁时长，期间服务是彻底关着的。
误解：分片数一变，取模结果对大部分 key 都会落到不同分片，不是只动一半。
误解：换 hash 函数只改「该去哪找」，数据本身还躺在旧分片上，找不到。
误解：这个方案的前提就是停服，没有双写也没有缓冲，写请求直接被拒。
optionExplanations_en: Once the mapping changes every row must be moved, dataset size sets the duration, and the service is fully closed throughout.
Misconception: changing the shard count sends most keys to a different shard under modulo, not just half of them.
Misconception: swapping the hash function only changes where you look; the data still sits on the old shards and is not found.
Misconception: this plan is defined by going offline — there is no dual write and no buffer, so writes are simply rejected.

scenario: 同一次 8→16 分片扩容，业务要求迁移期间不停服、不丢任何写。
scenario_en: The same 8-to-16 shard expansion, but the business requires zero downtime and zero lost writes during migration.
q: 生产环境该怎么迁这批数据？
q_en: How should production migrate this data?
options: 渐进迁移：迁移期间向新旧分片双写，读优先走新分片
先把流量整体切到新分片，再后台把旧数据慢慢补过去，读写都只打新分片
只对新写入使用新分片，旧数据永远留在旧分片上，不做任何迁移动作
对全库加只读锁，边搬边只允许读，搬完之后再统一放开写入口
options_en: Gradual migration: dual-write to both old and new shards during the move, and read with preference for the new shard
Cut all traffic to the new shards first, then backfill old data in the background while reads and writes hit only the new shards
Send only new writes to the new shards and leave old data on the old shards forever, migrating nothing
Take a read-only lock on the whole database, allow reads while copying, then reopen writes when the copy finishes
why: 正常双写期：一条写同时落新旧分片，后台按批搬历史数据；读优先新分片、未命中回落旧分片；搬完再停双写。代价是迁移期写放大一倍且逻辑更复杂。
why_en: During dual-write each write lands on both old and new shards while history is copied in batches; reads prefer the new shard and fall back to the old, and dual-write stops once the copy completes — at double write cost and extra complexity.
tradeoff: 不停机可用性 vs 迁移期双倍写开销与复杂度
whenOtherWins: 如果数据集很小、又有天然低峰维护窗口，直接停机 rehash 更简单，不用维护双写与回落逻辑。

termDefinitions.meaning: 迁移期间同一条写同时发往旧分片和新分片，保证两边都不缺数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dual write sends each write to both the old and the new shard during migration so neither side misses data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在服务持续可用的前提下分批把数据搬到新分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gradual migration copies data to new shards in batches while the service stays available.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读新分片未命中时再去旧分片读一次的兜底路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fallback read goes to the old shard when the new shard misses, as a safety path during migration.

optionExplanations: 双写保证迁移期不丢新数据，读优先新分片让流量随搬迁进度自然切过去。
误解：先切流量再补数据，中间读到的都是还没搬来的空洞，用户看到数据消失。
误解：旧数据永不迁移会让旧分片继续承担全部旧键的读写，热点一点没缓解。
误解：只读锁等于禁写，业务要求的是不停机写入，这条正好违反需求。
optionExplanations_en: Dual write guarantees no new data is lost, and preferring the new shard on reads shifts traffic naturally as the copy progresses.
Misconception: cutting traffic before backfilling means reads hit holes that have not arrived yet, so users see data disappear.
Misconception: never migrating old data leaves the old shards serving all old keys, so the hotspot is not relieved at all.
Misconception: a read-only lock is a write freeze, which directly violates the zero-downtime write requirement.

scenario: 分区键选得很好，推文均匀铺在各分片上；但一条病毒推文单独收到 10 万赞/秒，全都更新它自己的计数。
scenario_en: The partition key is well chosen and tweets spread evenly across shards, yet one viral tweet alone takes 100,000 likes per second, all updating its own counter.
q: 这条推文会造成什么问题？
q_en: What problem does this single tweet create?
options: 它的赞全落在同一个 key、同一个分片上，专用一整个分片也扛不住
问题会自动消失，因为好的分区键保证不会出现单点热度倾斜情况
只有读会变慢，写入因为已经均匀分布所以完全不会受到任何影响
所有分片会被同等拖慢，因为热 key 的写入会在集群内广播复制一遍
options_en: All its likes hit one key on one shard, and even dedicating an entire shard to it is not enough
The problem disappears on its own, because a good partition key rules out single-point skew
Only reads slow down; writes are already evenly spread so they are unaffected
Every shard slows equally, because writes to a hot key get broadcast and replicated cluster-wide
why: 分区键只保证 key 之间均匀，管不了单个 key 内部的热度：10 万赞/秒全打向同一个计数 key，落在唯一一个分片上，继续加分片也没用。
why_en: A partition key only balances across keys, never inside one: 100,000 likes per second all target the same counter key on a single shard, so adding shards changes nothing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单个键承受远超平均的读写流量，成为整个分片的瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key taking far more traffic than average, bottlenecking its whole shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落到哪个分片的字段，选得好才能均匀分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the field deciding which shard a record lands on; a good one spreads load evenly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流量或数据在分片之间分布不均，个别分片远高于平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Skew is uneven distribution of traffic or data across shards, leaving some far above average.

optionExplanations: 一个 key 只能属于一个分片，键内热度再高也无法靠增加分片数摊开。
误解：分区键管的是键之间的分布，单个键自身爆红它无能为力。
误解：10 万次/秒的计数更新就是写，写入正是被打爆的那一侧。
误解：写只落在这个 key 所属的分片，不会向全集群广播，其它分片依旧空闲。
optionExplanations_en: A key belongs to exactly one shard, so no amount of extra shards spreads heat that lives inside a single key.
Misconception: the partition key governs distribution between keys and can do nothing when one key itself goes viral.
Misconception: 100,000 counter updates per second are writes — the write side is precisely what is overwhelmed.
Misconception: the writes land only on that key shard and are not broadcast cluster-wide; the other shards stay idle.

scenario: 为解决 10 万赞/秒的热 key，团队在「所有 key 一律固定拆 k 份」和「只对检测到的热 key 动态拆 100 份」之间选。
scenario_en: To survive a 100,000-likes-per-second hot key, the team weighs splitting every key into a fixed k parts against dynamically splitting only detected hot keys into 100 sub-keys.
q: 两种拆键方案的关键差别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between the two key-splitting schemes?
options: 固定拆全部 key：实现最简单，但数据集和读放大都变成 k 倍
固定拆全部 key：只影响热 key 的存储，冷 key 完全不受任何影响
动态拆热 key：需要先重新选一次分区键，属于停机级别的大改动
动态拆热 key：只对可聚合数据无效，对用户资料这类原子数据才有效
options_en: Splitting every key: simplest to implement, but the dataset and read amplification both grow k times
Splitting every key: it only affects storage of hot keys, cold keys are untouched
Dynamic hot-key splitting: it requires choosing a new partition key first, a downtime-level change
Dynamic hot-key splitting: it fails for aggregatable data and works only for atomic data like user profiles
why: 固定拆 k 份把每个 key 的写量降到 1/k，代价是全库数据量乘 k、每次读要查 k 个子键；动态拆只让热 key 付这份代价，但要额外做热度检测。
why_en: A fixed k-way split cuts per-key write volume to one k-th but multiplies dataset size and per-read lookups by k, while dynamic splitting confines that cost to hot keys at the price of hotness detection.
tradeoff: 统一拆键的实现简单 vs 动态拆键的精准与检测复杂度
whenOtherWins: 如果小的 k 就能把写量拉回数据库容量内，固定拆全部 key 更省事，不必上热度检测那套逻辑。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个热 key 拆成 post1Likes-0 到 -(k-1) 这样的多个分片键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sub-keys split one hot key into several keys such as post1Likes-0 through post1Likes-(k-1).

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑读需要发出的实际读请求数量，拆 k 份就要读 k 次再求和。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read amplification is how many physical reads one logical read costs; a k-way split means k reads plus a sum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写者靠本地统计判断某个 key 是否已成为热 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hotness detection is writers using local statistics to decide whether a key has become hot.

optionExplanations: 写量降到 1/k 是收益，数据量和读次数同时乘 k 就是这条路统一付出的代价。
误解：这个方案的定义就是所有 key 一律拆，冷 key 同样膨胀 k 倍。
误解：拆子键是在同一套分区键之上加后缀，不需要重选分区键更不用停机。
误解：方向反了，拆键只对可聚合的计数有效，原子数据才是它不适用的那类。
optionExplanations_en: Cutting write volume to one k-th is the gain; multiplying dataset size and read count by k is the flat price this path pays.
Misconception: this scheme is defined by splitting every key, so cold keys inflate k-fold as well.
Misconception: sub-keys are suffixes on top of the existing partition key — no new partition key and no downtime.
Misconception: this reverses it — splitting works for aggregatable counters, and atomic data is the case it cannot serve.

scenario: 团队想把「拆成子键、读时求和」这招推广到所有热数据：点赞数、播放量、账户余额，还有用户资料。
scenario_en: The team wants to apply the split-into-sub-keys-and-sum-on-read trick to all hot data: like counts, view counts, account balances, and user profiles.
q: 这招对哪一类数据不成立？
q_en: For which kind of data does this trick not hold?
options: 用户资料：必须整体原子读写，拆成子键后无法靠求和还原
播放量：累加型指标，拆键后子键求和会重复计数导致结果偏大
账户余额：数值型数据，拆键会让余额精度出现累积误差的问题
点赞数：写入频率最高，因此最不适合用拆键这种方式来分摊压力
options_en: User profiles: they must be read and written atomically, and summing sub-keys cannot reconstruct them
View counts: an additive metric where summing sub-keys double-counts and overstates the total
Account balances: numeric data where splitting introduces accumulating precision errors
Like counts: the highest write frequency, which makes them the worst fit for split-based spreading
why: 拆键靠「所有子键求和 = 真值」成立，只适用于可聚合指标（赞、浏览、计数、余额）；用户资料这类必须原子读写的数据拆开后拼不回来。
why_en: Splitting works only when summing all sub-keys reproduces the truth, which holds for aggregatable metrics like likes, views, counts, and balances but not for data that must stay atomic such as user profiles.
tradeoff: 可聚合指标的写量分摊 vs 原子数据的完整性
whenOtherWins: 如果用户资料真的写压力极大，正确做法是按字段做垂直分区，而不是把同一份资料拆成子键求和。

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以把多份部分结果相加还原成真值的数值，如计数和余额。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregatable metric is a value whose partial results can be summed back into the true value, like counts and balances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整条记录必须一次性整体读到或写入，不能拆成互不相干的碎片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Atomic read/write means a record must be read or written as one whole and cannot be split into unrelated fragments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列/字段把一张表拆成多张，各自按访问模式优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical partitioning splits a table by columns into several tables, each optimized for its own access pattern.

optionExplanations: 资料的字段不是可相加的量，拆开后既没法求和也破坏了一次读到完整记录的语义。
误解：播放量是标准的可聚合指标，各子键各自计数，求和恰好等于真值。
误解：余额也是可聚合的，各子键存部分金额相加即可，与浮点精度不是一回事。
误解：写入频率高正是要拆键的理由，不是不适用的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Profile fields are not additive quantities, so sub-keys can neither be summed nor preserve read-the-whole-record semantics.
Misconception: view counts are a textbook aggregatable metric — each sub-key counts its share and the sum is exact.
Misconception: balances are aggregatable too, with each sub-key holding part of the amount; this is not a floating-point precision issue.
Misconception: high write frequency is the reason to split, not a reason the technique fails.

scenario: 写者检测到热 key 后开始写子键 post1Likes-0..99，但读者仍只读原 key post1Likes，页面上的赞数于是几乎不涨。
scenario_en: Writers detect a hot key and start writing sub-keys post1Likes-0 through -99, but readers still read only post1Likes, so the like count on the page barely moves.
q: 生产上通常怎么让读写双方对齐？
q_en: How do production systems usually keep readers and writers in agreement?
options: 读者永远查所有子键；写者靠本地统计检测热点后条件性写子键
写者向所有读者广播 split 公告，全部确认收到之后才执行拆分动作
让读者定期扫描数据库里的全部 key，发现子键命名就自动切换读法
把子键数量写死在配置文件里，靠人工同步发布来保证两边一致就行
options_en: Readers always check every sub-key, while writers use local statistics to conditionally write sub-keys once a key looks hot
Writers broadcast a split announcement to all readers and only execute the split after everyone acknowledges
Readers periodically scan all keys in the database and switch read strategy when they spot sub-key naming
Hard-code the sub-key count in a config file and rely on coordinated manual releases to keep both sides consistent
why: 读写不对齐会直接漏数：多数生产系统选「读者恒查所有子键」这条简单路，代价是固定的读放大。面试里别过度设计广播协议。
why_en: Any disagreement silently loses counts, so most production systems take the simple route of readers always checking every sub-key, paying a constant read amplification — do not over-engineer a broadcast protocol in an interview.
tradeoff: 固定读放大换实现简单 vs 广播协议换读效率
whenOtherWins: 当 k 很大、读 QPS 又极高，固定读放大的成本盖过一切时，写者广播 split 公告才值得那份复杂度。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写者通知所有读者「某个 key 已被拆成子键」的协调消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A split announcement is the coordination message writers send to tell every reader that a key has been split into sub-keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑读需要发出的实际读请求数量，拆 k 份就要读 k 次再求和。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read amplification is how many physical reads one logical read costs; a k-way split means k reads plus a sum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量读请求速率的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or queries per second, measures the rate of read requests a system handles.

optionExplanations: 读者无条件查全部子键，写者拆不拆都读得到，代价只是恒定的 k 倍读。
这条更高效但要等所有读者确认，任何一个读者掉线都会卡住拆分，复杂度高得多。
误解：全量扫 key 的开销远大于直接多读几个子键，而且发现拆分总是滞后的。
误解：靠人工发布对齐会在灰度期间出现读写版本不一致，正是漏数的根源。
optionExplanations_en: Readers unconditionally check every sub-key, so it works whether or not the writer split, costing only a constant k-fold read.
This is more efficient but must wait for every reader to acknowledge; one unreachable reader stalls the split, which is far more complex.
Misconception: scanning all keys costs far more than a few extra sub-key reads, and discovery always lags the actual split.
Misconception: coordinating by manual release leaves reader and writer versions mismatched during rollout, which is exactly how counts get lost.
